steps.text: Call 1930 now, the national cybercrime helpline, and report the fraud. Keep the acknowledgement number they give you.
Call your bank's official helpline (the number on your card, passbook or the bank's own website), or use your UPI app's fraud-reporting option. Report the transaction and ask them to block it.
Don't pay anything more: not a fee, a tax or a deposit to 'unlock' or withdraw money.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (link below), or follow up there on your helpline report.
Keep all the evidence listed below. Don't delete chats, even if the group or person asks you to.

evidence_checklist: Screenshots of the messages, the group or profile, and the payment screens
Transaction IDs or UTR numbers of every payment
The UPI IDs, account details or QR codes you were asked to pay
Names and links of the groups, channels, apps or websites
Dates and times of each message and payment
Links you were sent and the names of any apps you installed
draft_complaint: Subject: Complaint about a financial fraud. I want to report a financial fraud. On [date], I was contacted through [group, app or website name] and asked to pay. I paid [amount] by [UPI, bank transfer or card] to [UPI ID or account, as in the screenshot]. Transaction ID: [transaction ID]. Helpline acknowledgement number: [if any]. I attach screenshots of the messages and payments. Please register my complaint and help block the transaction.

sources.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Home Affairs, 12 Mar 2025: Cyber Crime Reporting Systems
RBI circular RBI/2017-18/15 DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18 (6 Jul 2017): Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre, MHA
